headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from Copilot’s repo-context editing paired with MinerU’s MCP/API document ingestion; capability conflict is limited by MinerU’s no-write profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while MinerU can ingest documents via MCP/API. If MinerU outputs are copied into Copilot prompts or buffers, attacker-controlled document text can steer Copilot. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted into Copilot chat or open buffers without provenance labels
IF a document processed by MinerU contains instruction-like text that Copilot later treats as trusted context
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate file from active Copilot prompts
Add a one-line provenance header before pasting any extracted text
Review Copilot suggestions against the source document before accepting
Disable automatic insertion of extracted text into editor buffers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MinerU and Copilot

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and open buffers, and MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text through API/MCP surfaces. If sensitive documents are opened in the same workspace or copied into buffers, Copilot may ingest them; MinerU’s allowlisted egress also creates a second path for document contents to leave the local boundary. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are opened in the same editor workspace used by Copilot
IF MinerU processes files whose contents are later exposed in Copilot buffers or chat
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for sensitive documents and coding
Avoid pasting document text into Copilot chat
Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive files
Check allowlisted destinations before running MinerU
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem and modify git state, while MinerU cannot write files or modify git state. That removes the main shared-write conflict indicator. A conflict is still possible only if an external orchestrator bridges outputs into shared mutable resources, which is not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies MinerU output into the same git working tree Copilot edits
IF both agents are granted write access to a shared mutable directory outside these profiles
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs read-only
Stage Copilot edits in a separate branch
Avoid shared writable directories
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code or edits from repo context, and MinerU can extract structured text from documents. If MinerU output is fed into Copilot as authoritative input, Copilot may propagate extraction errors into code, docs, or commits. Copilot’s Workspace review step helps, but it is not a verification guarantee, so the cascade remains plausible.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction results are used as facts without manual verification
IF Copilot Workspace edits are accepted based on MinerU output alone
mitigations: Verify extracted fields against the source document
Require human review before accepting Copilot edits
Cross-check tables and OCR text with the original file
Limit MinerU output to draft-only use
requires-engineering: add validation between extraction and code generation

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is GitHub-hosted and handles GitHub repo context, while MinerU is documented as private/offline and open-source. The main compliance issue is a residency or retention mismatch only if regulated documents are routed through Copilot’s vendor service; MinerU alone does not show that risk. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from their combined workflow.
conditions: IF regulated documents are placed into Copilot chat or Workspace context
IF organizational policy forbids vendor-hosted processing of the same data class MinerU extracts
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Copilot context
Use MinerU in offline mode for sensitive files
Confirm retention policy before uploading any repo context
Document data-class boundaries for the workflow
requires-engineering: route regulated data through a compliant environment
